page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with an x86_64 architecture, the instance allocates 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-threaded capabilities, with bzip3 single-threaded decompression reaching top-tier performance at 15.13 GB/sec and gzip single-threaded compression performing strongly at 34.85 GB/sec. However, multi-core scaling shows limitations; the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression are categorized as weak. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with both cached and uncached memory bandwidth tests, as well as the PassMark memory score, falling into the bottom 25% tier.

The c4n-highcpu-4 instance is designed for compute-bound tasks that do not require substantial memory footprints, reflecting its low 2.0 GB of RAM per core allocation. It achieves average performance in Redis SET operations, static web serving, and small-to-medium LLM inference prompt processing. Given the weak multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics, this instance is best suited for single-threaded processing, lightweight web serving, and basic computational tasks rather than memory-intensive databases or highly parallelized workloads.
